identity.author: John Davenant
identity.work: Two Dissertations (De praedestinatione through Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol partial)
identity.edition: Dissertationes duae (Cambridge: Roger Daniel, 1650). Partial through Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol (first incommodum). Arg. 14 Sol cont. (second incommodum / Christ-order) remains.

scope.locus: De praedestinatione Cap. IX Arg. 14 religion-foundation / Corvinus.
scope.next_locus: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont. (second incommodum; Arminius on Christ ordered after election / love of justice).

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 (Corvinus): our sentence overturns religion's foundation two ways — precise election without obedience-intuit loves men more than justice and kills all religious solicitude
english: That assumed, they try to show our view overturns religion's foundation in two ways. First: it sets God as having precisely elected some to salvation without any gaze upon obedience — from which it follows that God loved those men more than his own justice. That granted, the necessity of rendering obedience is taken away, and all care about religion.
sections.latin: Hoc posito conantur ostendere sententiam nostram hoc fundamentum religionis duplici modo evertere. Primo, quia statuit Deum sine ullius obedientiae intuitu aliquos praecise ad salutem elegisse: unde sequitur, Deum illos homines magis amasse quam justitiam suam: Quo posito, tollitur obedientiae praestandae necessitas omnisque de religione solicitudo.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 (Corvinus): second way — reprobation to damnation without gaze on disobedience hates the creature without justice-love and kills hope in God
english: Second: as they say, it sets God as having predestined some men to damnation without any gaze on disobedience — from which again it follows that God hates his creature with no necessity arising from love of justice. That granted, hope in God is taken away. For whoever is sure he has been reprobated from salvation apart from any gaze on sin will believe nothing can profit him, however hard he strives to avoid sin.
sections.latin: Secundo, quia (ut illi aiunt) statuit Deus aliquos homines ad damnationem praedestinasse sine intuitu inobedientiae: unde rursus sequitur, Deum creaturam suam odisse citra nullam ex amore erga justitiam necessitatem: Quo posito, tollitur spes in Deum. Qui enim certe sibi persuadet se a salute citra peccati intuitum esse reprobatum, credet nihil sibi posse prodesse, quomodocunque studeat peccatum vitare.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 (Corvinus): both inconveniences charged because we teach precise will to save before satisfaction in Christ / faith-foresight, and will to damn apart from impenitence
english: They contend that both inconveniences follow from our view. Why? Because we teach that God so loved certain sinners that he precisely willed to save them before he satisfied his love of justice in Christ, or before he looked on them as believing in Christ. And on the other side, we teach that God wills to damn certain sinners apart from considering impenitence — even though he has satisfied his justice in Christ.
sections.latin: Utrumque hoc incommodum ex nostra sententia sequi contendunt, quia docemus, Deum quosdam peccatores ita amasse, ut praecise eos voluerit servare, antequam amori suo erga justitiam satisfecerit in Christo, aut eos ut in Christum credentes sit intuitus; atque e contra, Deum quosdam peccatores velle damnare citra considerationem impoenitentiae, licet justitiae suae in Christo Deus satisfecerit.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: grave charge — if our sentence uproots Christianity's foundations it must itself be uprooted; we grant their double-love foundation but deny our sentence fights it
english: Truly this charge against us is grave. If our view uproots Christianity's foundations, it must itself be torn up from the roots. So let us weigh how true the accusation is. First: we pick no quarrel with the adversaries over that twofold love in which they set religion's foundation — but we deny that our view fights that love.
sections.latin: Grave profecto hoc crimen est quod nobis objicitur. Nam si sententia nostra convellat religionis Christianae fundamenta, est ipsa quidem ab imis fundamentis revellenda. Expendamus igitur quam vera sit haec criminatio. Atque inprimis non intendimus ullam litem adversariis de duplici illo amore in quo religionis fundamentum collocant; sed negamus sententiam nostram huic amori repugnare.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: two alleged inconveniences of precise election without obedience-gaze — loves predestined more than justice; kills necessity of faith, obedience, and religious care
english: They press that we set God as having precisely elected some to salvation without any gaze on obedience. That opinion, they think, is pressed by two inconveniences. One: it makes God love those so predestined more than his own justice, because he wills to save them before he has satisfied his love of justice in Christ, or foresaw them as believing in Christ. The other: it takes away all need of faith and obedience, and all care for religion, because we say those so predestined are loved by God unto salvation before and apart from foresight of faith and obedience in them.
sections.latin: Instant, nos statuere Deum sine ullius obedientiae intuitu aliquos praecise ad salutem elegisse: Quam opinionem duobus incommodis urgeri arbitrantur. Unum est, quod ponat Deum taliter praedestinatos magis amare quam justitiam suam, quia vult eos servare, antequam amori suo erga justitiam satisfecerit in Christo, aut eos ut in Christo credentes praeviderit. Alterum est, quod tollat omnem necessitatem fidei et obedientiae, omnemque religionis solicitudinem, quia dicimus taliter praedestinatos amari a Deo ad salutem ante et citra praevisionem fidei et obedientiae in iisdem.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: difference from Arminius — not that elect can be saved while remaining unbelieving, but that faith/obedience is not antecedent election-motive from free will determining itself
english: I answer: Our view does not differ from the Arminian in this — that he holds the elect cannot be saved without faith and obedience rendered, while we think they can be saved even if they stay unbelieving and rebellious to God. The difference is this: he makes that condition of faith and obedience an antecedent motive of election, and hangs the act of believing on free choice excited by God's grace and as it were brought to a certain balance, yet determining itself before election and thereby procuring divine election.
sections.latin: Respondeo: Non in eo situm est discrimen sententiae nostrae ab Arminiana, quod ille electos non posse salvari statuat absque praestita fidei et obedientiae conditione, nos autem opinemur eos servari posse etiamsi maneant infideles et Deo rebelles: sed quod ille hanc fidei et obedientiae conditionem facit antecedaneum electionis motivum, et hunc actum credendi suspendit a libero arbitrio per gratiam Dei excitato et quasi ad aequilibrium quoddam reducto, sed seipsum ante electionem determinante, et inde electionem Divinam procurante.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: we judge faith/obedience necessary to eternal life by fixed decree — yet as special gift prepared in predestination, produced by special operation, foreseen as medium not motive
english: We take the other side. For adults we judge faith and obedience plainly necessary to everlasting life by God's fixed decree. Yet we deny that this faith and obedience was foreseen in this or that person as something springing from free choice stirred by common grace, and then dragging election's benefit after it. We hold instead that it was a special gift, prepared from eternity for each elect person in the predestination decree. It is to be produced from the human will by a special operation that depends on that decree. From eternity, then, it was foreseen in all the elect — not as the motive by which they win their election, but as the preceding medium by which they reach the kingdom of heaven to which they were elect.
sections.latin: Nos e contra, quamvis fidei et obedientiae conditionem (si de adultis loquamur) ad vitam aeternam consequendam, ex Dei fixo decreto plane necessariam judicemus, tamen agnoscimus hanc fidem et obedientiam non praevisam fuisse in hac aut illa singulari persona, tanquam ex libero ejus arbitrio per gratiam communem excitato enascentem, et electionis beneficium post se trahentem; sed tanquam speciale donum fuisse huic et illi singulari personae in decreto praedestinationis ab aeterno praeparatum, et ex humana voluntate speciali quadam operatione ab eodem decreto dependente producendam, et inde ab aeterno praevisam in omnibus electis, non tanquam motivum quo ipsi consequantur suam electionem, sed tanquam medium quo praecedente consequentur regnum caelorum ad quod fuerunt electi.

sections.title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol: first inconvenience fails — electing Peter/Paul to infallible share of Christ before foreseeing free will inclined is supreme love of justice, not loving them more than justice
english: That premised, our view is not caught in those two inconveniences. Not the first: God is not charged with loving Peter or Paul more than his own justice if from eternity he elected and designated them to infallible share in Christ, faith, and salvation before he foresaw their free choice efficaciously and perseveringly inclined — through the offer of sufficient grace — to embrace Christ, conceive faith, and take the way of salvation. Nay, this argues supreme love of justice in God: that Peter and Paul, whom of mere mercy he loved exceedingly unto salvation, he yet would not lead to that destined salvation unless such means were used by which his justice would first be satisfied.
sections.latin: Hoc praemisso, sententia nostra praedictis duobus incommodis haud implicatur. Non priore; Quia Deus non arguitur magis amasse Petrum aut Paulum quam suam justitiam, si illos ab aeterno elegit et designavit ad infallibilem participationem Christi, fidei, et salutis, antequam praevidit liberum illorum arbitrium per oblationem gratiae sufficientis ad Christum amplexandum, fidem concipiendam, salutisque viam capiessendam, efficaciter et perseveranter inclinatum. Imo hoc arguit summum amorem justitiae in Deo, quod Petrum et Paulum, quos ad salutem ex mera misericordia eximie dilexit, noluerit tamen ad hanc salutem illis destinatam perducere nisi talibus mediis adhibitis quibus justitiae suae prius satisfaceret.
